newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 1.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 1.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

NAB's U.S. ADRS closed down 1 1/14 at 61 7/8 on New York overnight as the U.S. 30 year treasury yield climbed to 7.10 percent. Locally, the June 10 year bond future contract was down 15 at 91.755 just prior to stock market open and the physical bond yield rose to 8.18 percent from 8.03 percent.

Optus Communications said early on Friday it had agreed with US West, PBL and Seven to buy them out of their Optus Vision shares in exchange for Optus Communications convertible note that can be converted to shares at or after Optus' float. The deal will also see Mayne increase its Optus stake to 26.1 percent. All legal action has been dropped. Seven said later it would spend A$62.5 million to buy 50 million shares in Optus.

ANZ Grindlays Bank was awarded $240 million by an Indian arbitration panel for money forfeited by the bank in the wake of a share scandal that rocked the country's stock markets in 1992, a senior official of the bank said on Sunday in Bombay. Banking analysts were reported in the Financial Review saying the award would produce windfall profits of A$50 million for the bank.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday its North American copper costs were running at an average of 80 U.S. cents a pound, up from before BHP's Magma acquisition. BHP also said it would struggle to reduce that cost in the current quarter.
